lines.en: Please select a song from the menu before proceeding.
lines.zh: 请在继续之前从菜单中选择一首歌。

lines.en: menu:
Goodnight
lines.zh: 晚安

lines.en: Hallelujah
lines.zh: Hallelujah

lines.en: Little Bunny
lines.zh: 小兔子

lines.en: No Music
lines.zh: 无音乐

lines.en: Thank you for your assistance.
lines.zh: 感谢您的协助。

lines.en: We apologize for the inconvenience and are diligently working to make this a better product for future use.
lines.zh: 我们为给您带来的不便致歉，并正在努力将其打造成未来更好用的产品。

lines.en: The event will now begin.
lines.zh: 活动即将开始。

lines.en: scene black
But your pain will be eternal.
lines.zh: 但你的痛苦将是永恒的。

lines.en: Praise be to the Wishing Well.
lines.zh: 赞美许愿井。

lines.en: Signed — {i}the one who drowned in it.{/i}
lines.zh: 署名——{i}溺死在井里的那个人。{/i}

lines.en: scene boysdontcry1
There are different people in different places who handle their grief in different ways.
lines.zh: 不同的人在不同的地方，以不同的方式处理自己的悲伤。

lines.en: If that’s not something you’ve garnered from Christmas this year, I’m not sure what to tell you.
lines.zh: 如果这都不是你从今年圣诞节里领会到的东西，那我不知道该跟你说什么。

lines.en: Either you’ve not been paying attention or, like the former hero, you’re too distressed to think. And I suppose I wouldn’t blame you for that after all this time under the red-hot sun.
lines.zh: 要么是你没在注意，要么就是像那位前英雄一样，你痛苦得无法思考。而我想，在炽热的太阳下熬了这么久，我也不会为此责怪你。

lines.en: But, whatever the case, I’m telling you the truth. And I want you to know that, should it all end right now — should you vanish off the face of this earth, there is someone who will miss you.
lines.zh: 但无论如何，我告诉你的都是实话。而我想让你知道：如果一切就在此时结束——如果你从这地球上消失，总会有人想念你。

lines.en: It’s doubtful they’d break into someone’s house to come to your aid — those actions are reserved for the most foolish of fools.
lines.zh: 他们大概不会闯进别人家来救你——那种举动是留给最蠢的蠢货的。

lines.en: But chances are, there’d be someone curled up in a ball on their bed...or hunched over the counter at a local bar, contemplating whether or not there’s something they can do to help.
lines.zh: 但很可能，会有某个人蜷成一团躺在床上……或者趴在附近酒吧的吧台上，琢磨着自己能不能做点什么来帮忙。

lines.en: And maybe there is. Maybe there isn’t. The answer to such a question is for you to decide, not me.
lines.zh: 也许有，也许没有。这个问题的答案该由你来决定，不是我。

lines.en: It’s like choosing a song or setting a character’s profile costume. It’s something that matters to {i}you,{/i} but won’t make much sense to anyone else.
lines.zh: 这就像选一首歌，或者设置一个角色的资料服装。这件事对{i}你{/i}很重要，但对别人没什么意义。

lines.en: They can acknowledge what you find important. And they can go out of their way to try and empathize or sympathize or whichever one they’re capable of, but they’ll never see what you see when you look down.
lines.zh: 他们可以承认你觉得重要的东西。也可以特意去尝试共情或同情，或者随便他们能做到哪一种，但他们永远看不到你低头时所看到的东西。

lines.en: They don’t know how your shoes feel. They don’t know what sort of insoles you’re wearing or the shape of the blisters formed between your toes from chasing after fulfillment for far too long.
lines.zh: 他们不知道你的鞋穿起来是什么感觉。他们不知道你垫的是什么样的鞋垫，也不知道你为了追逐满足感太久，脚趾间磨出的水泡是什么形状。

lines.en: But that doesn’t change how they’d wrap you in gauze if those blisters popped. It doesn’t change how they’d apply infection-fighting ointment to your open wounds to prevent the decay of your flesh.
lines.zh: 可这并不改变他们会在水泡破掉时为你裹上纱布的事实。也不改变他们会在你敞开的伤口上涂抗菌药膏、防止你的肉腐烂的事实。

lines.en: {i}This{/i} is what you’re meant to take from all of this.
lines.zh: {i}这{/i}才是你该从这一切里带走的东西。

lines.en: This is a moment of reprieve, where you and I can compare the sizes of our hands and laugh at how much we’ve grown since we were young.
lines.zh: 这是一个喘息的时刻，你和我可以比一比我们手的大小，再笑话自己从年少至今长了多少。

lines.en: These thoughts used to hurt us, and the honest truth is that they still hurt today. But we have gotten better at pretending to be fine when we’re not. And we know how to laugh now.
lines.zh: 这些念头曾经伤害过我们，而老实说，它们到今天依然伤人。但我们更擅长在自己并不好的时候假装没事了。而且我们现在会笑了。

lines.en: We just don’t do it as much as we used to. And while it hurts, it doesn’t {i}hurt{/i} as much as it used to.
lines.zh: 只是我们笑得不像以前那么多了。虽然还是会痛，但已经不像以前那么{i}痛{/i}了。

lines.en: Our first slide in tonight’s flashy display of poetic prowess comes to you from a poorly named bar just a few miles away from the home of the former hero.
lines.zh: 今晚这场华丽的诗艺展示中，我们的第一张幻灯片来自一家名字起得很糟的酒吧，就在那位前英雄家几英里外。

lines.en: Sara Sakakibara had drained this month’s profits at a local strip of outlet shops this morning, knowing well that whatever she bought would collect dust in her living room for an undetermined amount of time.
lines.zh: Sara Sakakibara 今天上午在本地一条奥特莱斯商业街上，把这个月的利润花了个精光，她心里很清楚，不管买了什么，都会在客厅里积上不知多久的灰。

lines.en: But she was okay with that.
lines.zh: 但她对此无所谓。

lines.en: It wasn’t like the first time. She knew {i}this{/i} one would come back. And despite the similarities between the two men, which grew ever more prevalent with each passing day, she had faith.
lines.zh: 这跟第一次不一样。她知道{i}这一{/i}个会回来。尽管这两个男人之间的相似之处随着日子一天天过去越来越明显，她仍然有信心。

lines.en: But she wasn’t sure when such a thing returned to her.
lines.zh: 可她不确定这份东西是什么时候回到她身上的。

lines.en: When she was younger, she believed in God.
lines.zh: 她更小的时候，是信上帝的。

lines.en: It wasn’t until the fifth time her father beat her that she’d given up that belief. And while it could have lasted longer had he not chipped her tooth that night, she was happy to finally be rid of divinity.
lines.zh: 直到父亲第五次打她，她才放弃了那份信仰。虽然如果那晚他没有打缺她的牙，这份信仰或许还能维持得更久些，但她很高兴终于摆脱了神性。

lines.en: It gave her more time to focus on what made {i}her{/i} happy.
lines.zh: 这给了她更多时间去专注于让{i}她{/i}开心的东西。

lines.en: Unfortunately, that meant more time to realize that not very many things {i}did{/i} that.
lines.zh: 不幸的是，那也意味着有更多时间意识到，能让她开心的东西{i}其实{/i}并不多。

lines.en: So here she was, [[figuratively] alone on Christmas, praying to the God of Wine that all those sappy movies she used to watch this time of year would somehow spill out into reality.
lines.zh: 于是她就这样，在圣诞节[[figuratively] 孤身一人，向酒神祈祷，希望她往年这个时候看的那些煽情电影能以某种方式溢出到现实里。

lines.en: But they didn’t.
lines.zh: 可它们没有。

lines.en: scene black
He didn’t come this year.
lines.zh: 他今年没来。

lines.en: And, at this point in time, it was uncertain if he’d come next year as well.
lines.zh: 而到了这个时候，他明年会不会来也不确定。

lines.en: Her reincarnated fate stayed propped up, but porous.
lines.zh: 她那转世而来的命运依然被支撑着，却千疮百孔。

lines.en: And she had a thought.
lines.zh: 于是她有了一个念头。

lines.en: That thought went something like this.
lines.zh: 那个念头大概是这样的。

lines.en: “I hope he sees the fireworks tonight.”
lines.zh: 「我希望他今晚能看到烟花。」

lines.en: There’s a pause as she sits on that thought.
lines.zh: 她停在这个念头上，沉默了一会儿。

lines.en: Then, another one comes.
lines.zh: 然后，又一个念头冒了出来。

lines.en: “Have I always been this weak?”
lines.zh: 「我一直都这么软弱吗？」

lines.en: scene boysdontcry2
Thankfully, there were people in other places faring a bit better than she was.
lines.zh: 好在，还有人在别的地方过得比她好一点。

lines.en: Which isn’t to say these people wouldn’t {i}also{/i} miss you if you one day ceased to be. For them, it might just take a little longer to set in.
lines.zh: 这并不是说，如果有一天你不在了，这些人就{i}不会{/i}想念你。对他们来说，也许只是需要更久一点才会反应过来。

lines.en: How they fit into this story apart from that remains a bit uncertain.
lines.zh: 除此之外，他们在这个故事里扮演什么角色，仍有些不确定。

lines.en: Unfortunately, AUTO-PILOT is unable to locate any applicable background information that would appear relevant to the themes being currently executed. As such, a new theme will be chosen.
lines.zh: 遗憾的是，AUTO-PILOT 无法找到任何与当前正在执行的主题相关的适用背景信息。因此，将选择一个新主题。

lines.en: AUTO-PILOT has selected “new beginnings” as all other options returned little to no results.
lines.zh: AUTO-PILOT 选择了「新的开始」，因为所有其他选项几乎没有返回任何结果。

lines.en: The relevance of this idea in relation to Akira Arakawa has little to do with his current mental state and everything to do with what comes next in his life without his lover.
lines.zh: 这个念头与 Akira Arakawa 的关联，跟他当前的精神状态关系不大，而完全关乎失去爱人之后他人生接下来的走向。

lines.en: All around him, new lives are beginning. And, in the strangest of places, they appear to be {i}thriving{/i} as well.
lines.zh: 在他周围，新的生命正在开始。而且，在最奇怪的地方，它们看上去也{i}生机勃勃{/i}。

lines.en: Kaori Kadowaki and the {b}ENTITY{/b} known as “Nao-chan” struggle to understand just what “Christmas” means.
lines.zh: Kaori Kadowaki 和那个被称为「Nao-chan」的{b}实体{/b}，正在费力理解「圣诞节」到底是什么意思。

lines.en: Their tiny apartment remains mostly undecorated, save the repeated scribbling of “Remember to Christmas” on a large dry-erase board hanging over the bed.
lines.zh: 她们那间小公寓基本没什么装饰，只有挂在床上方的一块大白板上，反复涂写着「记得过圣诞节」。

lines.en: Kaori would use this to remind herself of tasks that need to be completed or other important details she frequently overlooks.
lines.zh: Kaori 会用它来提醒自己那些需要完成的任务，或者其他她经常忽略的重要细节。

lines.en: But there was one important detail that {i}didn’t{/i} make it onto the board — today was her birthday.
lines.zh: 但有一样重要的细节{i}没有{/i}写上去——今天是她的生日。

lines.en: She had just turned 23. But age wasn’t a thing she typically thought of as it all seemed meaningless when humans far outlive most other mammals.
lines.zh: 她刚满 23 岁。不过她平时并不怎么想年龄，因为人类比大多数其他哺乳动物活得久得多，这似乎毫无意义。

lines.en: Lately, her thoughts had done naught but measure the outlines of the figures she cared the most for. And with one of those figures missing, it made it easier to focus on “Nao-chan.”
lines.zh: 最近，她的思绪除了描摹她最在乎的那些身影的轮廓之外什么也没做。而其中一个身影缺席了，这让她更容易把注意力放在「Nao-chan」身上。

lines.en: She’d begun to feel like a real mother — and it was the start of a relationship that, for the first time ever, she didn’t believe was teetering on the precipice of nonexistence.
lines.zh: 她开始觉得自己像个真正的母亲了——而这段关系，有史以来第一次，她不认为它正摇摇欲坠地悬在消亡的悬崖边。

lines.en: “Nao-chan” pets a small frog that was given to her as her very first Christmas present.
lines.zh: 「Nao-chan」抚摸着一只小青蛙，那是别人送给她的第一份圣诞礼物。

lines.en: The frog would not receive a name as A) she could not speak. And B) she didn’t realize she was supposed to give it one.
lines.zh: 这只青蛙不会得到名字，因为 A）她不会说话。而 B）她没意识到自己应该给它起一个。

lines.en: No other narration in regard to her thoughts or feelings can be divulged at this time.
lines.zh: 关于她的想法或感受，目前无法透露更多旁白。

lines.en: scene black
As the scene fades to black once more, a note from the desk of the ninth god falls into my hands.
lines.zh: 当画面再度淡入黑暗时，一张来自第九位神明书桌的便条落进了我手里。

lines.en: It reads the following.
lines.zh: 上面写着以下内容。

lines.en: “There will be no new beginnings.”
lines.zh: 「不会有新的开始。」

lines.en: “For the first time in years, the clocks have corrected themselves. And while they will not tick the way they did when we were younger, they’ll no longer get stuck at midnight.”
lines.zh: 「多年来第一次，时钟自我校准了。虽然它们不会再像我们年少时那样滴答作响，但它们再也不会卡在午夜了。」

lines.en: “The world will move, but it will not.”
lines.zh: 「世界会前进，但它不会。」

lines.en: “And he will grow, but he will not.”
lines.zh: 「而他会成长，但他不会。」

lines.en: “Watch him closely, like a zookeeper.”
lines.zh: 「像动物园管理员那样，紧紧盯着他。」

lines.en: “And prod him with your branding iron once he stops reacting to the peanuts tossed at his head by vicious onlookers.”
lines.zh: 「等他对那些恶毒旁观者朝他头上扔的花生不再有反应时，就用你的烙铁去戳他。」

lines.en: scene boysdontcry3
: I don’t understand. If the world is not yet full of light, how has the darkness gone?
lines.zh: : 我不明白。如果这世界还没有被光充满，黑暗怎么会消失？

lines.en: : What remains of the fraying rope? And whose are the hands that tug at it while Our Father sleeps in Underheaven?
lines.zh: : 那根磨损的绳子还剩下什么？当我们的父在 Underheaven 沉睡时，又是谁的手在拉扯它？

lines.en: : Who...is she talking to?
lines.zh: : 她在跟……谁说话？

lines.en: : Better question, what the hell is she doing here? My cool hangout spot is way less cool now that Yasu’s talking to ghosts in it.
lines.zh: : 更好的问题是，她到底在这儿干什么？我这个超酷的据点可一点都不酷了，因为 Yasu 正在里面跟鬼说话。

lines.en: : I mean...we don’t {i}know{/i} it’s a ghost. I had an imaginary friend when I was younger. I’m sure you did too, right?
lines.zh: : 我是说……我们又不{i}确定{/i}那是鬼。我小时候有个想象中的朋友。你肯定也有过吧？

lines.en: : I had an imaginary fuck buddy. Friends are for losers.
lines.zh: : 我有个想象中的炮友。朋友是给失败者准备的。

lines.en: : Watched?
lines.zh: : 被注视？

lines.en: : I was not watched.
lines.zh: : 我没有被注视。

lines.en: : I have done what was instructed of me. I have laid the foundation for our New Hope with my very own hands so that we may one day grow and flourish like an endless field of sunflowers.
lines.zh: : 我已经完成了被指示的一切。我亲手为我们的 New Hope 打下了地基，好让我们有朝一日能像一望无际的向日葵田那样生长、繁盛。

lines.en: : That is what you wanted, is it not?...So why will you give me no answers?
lines.zh: : 那不就是你想要的吗？……那你为什么不肯给我答案？

lines.en: : Why will you not bring him back? Do we not {i}need{/i} him anymore? Is he truly that broken?
lines.zh: : 你为什么不把他带回来？我们已经不{i}需要{/i}他了吗？他真的坏成那样了吗？

lines.en: : Uh...should we maybe, like...call out to her or something?
lines.zh: : 呃……我们要不要，那个……朝她喊一声什么的？

lines.en: : Sacrifice?...
: What {i}kind{/i} of sacrifice?
lines.zh: : 什么{i}样{/i}的献祭？

lines.en: : Yeah. I think we should do that.
lines.zh: : 是啊。我觉得我们该走了。

lines.en: scene boysdontcry4
: Yasu! Hey! What are you-
lines.zh: : Yasu！嘿！你在干——

lines.en: scene boysdontcry5
: Get out! You’re going to scare it away!
lines.zh: : 出去！你会把它吓跑的！

lines.en: : Scare what away, weirdo? You’re all alone down there.
lines.zh: : 吓跑什么啊，怪胎？下面明明就你一个人。

lines.en: : The Emissary of Pegasus! With wings of glass and eyes of lead! The courier who carries the cord! It only appears before those who are trusted to carry out its order!
lines.zh: : Pegasus 的使者！长着玻璃的翅膀和铅做的眼睛！携带绳索的信使！它只会显现在被托付去执行它命令的人面前！

lines.en: : Fuck it. I’m calling Touka. I’m not qualified to babysit her.
lines.zh: : 去他的。我要打电话给 Touka。我没资格看孩子。

lines.en: : Yasu...do you want to come with us for a little-
lines.zh: : Yasu……你要不要跟我们一起待一会儿——

lines.en: scene boysdontcry6
: No! I have to-
lines.zh: : 不！我必须——

lines.en: scene boysdontcry7
: Have to...
lines.zh: : 必须……

lines.en: scene black
: It’s gone...
lines.zh: : 它走了……

lines.en: scene boysdontcry8
The idea of new beginnings, as pointless at this point in time as they may sound, are wonderful in the sense that they open the door for new bouts of happiness.
lines.zh: 新的开始这个念头，尽管在此刻听来可能毫无意义，却有着美妙的一面：它为新一波幸福打开了大门。

lines.en: The downside is that slamming a door twice has a better chance of breaking its hinges than just doing it once.
lines.zh: 缺点是，把门摔两次比只摔一次更有可能把合页摔坏。

lines.en: Regardless, it’s a temptation that many can’t help but lean into as it eases the seemingly permanent suffering of knowing you missed out on obtaining something everyone else has.
lines.zh: 不管怎样，这是一种许多人都忍不住要投入其中的诱惑，因为它能缓解那种看似永恒的痛苦——知道自己错过了别人都拥有的东西。

lines.en: But what about those who are just {i}pretending{/i} to have it? What if we’re {i}all{/i} searching for something but don’t want to {i}admit{/i} that because it makes us look weak?
lines.zh: 可那些只是{i}假装{/i}拥有它的人呢？如果我们{i}所有人{/i}都在寻找某样东西，却因为那会让自己显得软弱而不愿{i}承认{/i}呢？

lines.en: There are people like this, people like Yumi Yamaguchi, who fear weakness more than anything.
lines.zh: 就有这样的人，比如 Yumi Yamaguchi 这样的人，她们最害怕的就是软弱。

lines.en: “Raised” under the unwatchful eye of the Yakuza by shonen manga and action movies, she’d grown accustomed to violence over the years. And she witnessed firsthand just how many problems it solved.
lines.zh: 在黑道疏于看管的眼皮底下，由少年漫画和动作片「抚养」长大，这些年来她早已习惯了暴力。而且她亲眼见证过暴力解决了多少问题。

lines.en: But that never made the crack of brass knuckles against a trembling lower jaw sound any less shocking. And it never cleaned the blood from severed pinkies off of the floor.
lines.zh: 可那从未让指虎砸在颤抖的下颌骨上的碎裂声变得不那么骇人。也从未把断掉的小指留下的血从地板上擦干净。

lines.en: Yet, here she was — submitting to the desires of a woman who never once desired {i}her.{/i} And she {i}knows{/i} she looks weak, but she learned from {i}you{/i} that that’s not all there is to someone.
lines.zh: 然而，她现在就在这里——臣服于一个从未渴望过{i}她{/i}的女人的欲望。而她{i}知道{/i}自己看起来很软弱，但她从{i}你{/i}身上学到：一个人并不只有这一面。

lines.en: Yes, {i}you.{/i} Not you, but {i}you.{/i}
